text:
marta: Heads-up — we need a short, ops-friendly checklist for quantized benchmark runs (FP8/INT8/4bit). Goal: reproduce perf numbers across infra + detect regressions. Outline suggestions below.

kevin: +1. key constraints: warmup behavior, GPU power capping, tokenization parity, kernel selection determinism, KV cache priming.

sam: throwing a draft command to capture the idea:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. ./bench/run.py \n  --model meta/llama2-13b \n  --precision int8 \n  --seq_len 1024 \n  --tokens_per_query 128 \n  --batch_size 8 \n  --warmup_steps 200 \n  --measure_samples 100 \n  --powercap 200 \n  --disable_dynamic_kernel_switching
```

jia: reproducibility note: always compare to a FP16 baseline using same runtime build + same CUDA/driver. Record driver/kernel versions in run_config.

marta: warmup specifics — 200 warmup steps is a starting point, but verify plateau via a perf timeline; for short-prompt distributions increase to 500. Warmup must include KV-cache priming by sending a few long-context requests (prefill).

kevin: tokenization parity — run tokenizer on full eval set and save token counts. Use exact same tokenizer binary+version. Store tokens artifact (tokenization.json).

sam: batching heuristics — for fair per-token latency comparisons: (a) disable variable-sized runtime batching, (b) run with fixed-batch (pad to max_seq in batch). Also produce one run with production "adaptive" batching to show delta.

marta: kernel selection — to make comparisons meaningful we should either pin kernel choices or at least log the chosen kernel per layer. Add a flag --dump-kernel-info to capture kernel ids and heuristics.

kevin: calibration effects — calibration artifacts change numerical behavior. For every quant run include: calib seed, dataset subset used, stats (min/max/scale) and for FP8 record exponent bias/format. Without these you can't repro accuracy/perf differences.

jia: perf regression detection — run nightly golden jobs (same model + token set). Compute per-sample latency P50/P95/P99, token/sec, and relative delta vs baseline. Auto-fail or create ticket if regressions >3% for critical metrics.

sam: power limits — lock GPU power cap and record clocks/temps. GPUs boost differently under different power caps; include a small sweep (150/180/200W) and record token/sec vs power.

marta: profiling — gather an nsys trace for at least one representative scenario plus lightweight event logs for all runs (cuda events). Annotate where time is spent: kernel execution, memcpy, kernel-selection overhead.

kevin: KV-cache behavior — measure cold-start (no cache) vs warm (prefill) incremental per-token latency. Make a tiny script that issues a long prefix and then measures per-token time as we stream.

marta: result packaging — required artifacts per run: run_config.json (flags & env), tokenization.json, kernel_info.json, calib_artifacts/*, nsys_trace/*.qdrep, lightweight_traces/*.json, aggregate_metrics.csv. Zip and upload to the bench bucket.

sam: ops note — CI should verify presence of required artifacts and fail if missing. Also keep a control run that disables quant-specific optimizations (to sanity-check correctness/perf).

jia: perf-bot: nightly benchmark finished: model=llama2-13b precision=int8 p50=18.3ms p95=42.1ms token/s=12.0 artifacts=gs://redwood-bench/1947325555

kevin: small TODO: add a normalizer to adjust for instance-level clock/driver differences (or at least tag results with driver/clock so we can filter). cc @infra.

marta: I'll draft a one-page ops checklist from this and push to docs/bench for sign-off. Thanks all :rocket:
